text:
Ashley: heads-up — saw EU fleet saturation this morning, streaming sessions accounting for most of the in-flight slots and pushing non-stream batch jobs into the >10s queue. queue_len=118 avg_wait=13.2s gpu_util=94% :grimacing:
Kevin: ouch. is that a single model or spread across variants? any tenant skew?
Ashley: mostly rwd-gpt-3.8-q4a on dedicated eu-west pools. roughly 60% of active requests were streaming sessions; avg open-stream-duration ~40s.
Maria: streaming keeps a slot + KV cache open which is the culprit. our admission currently treats stream/non-stream the same and only counts inflight requests, not estimated hold time.
Justin: quick thought — we need admission that is time-aware (or token-budget-aware). streaming should either reserve fractional slots or be downgraded when constrained.
Kevin: agreed. two simple levers: 1) separate queues (streaming lane vs fast batch lane) with per-lane capacity caps, 2) preemptive/downgrade path for streaming to non-stream chunked responses.
Ashley: we also hit scaling limits in eu-west due to provider quotas so autoscaler couldn't add GPUs fast enough — autoscaler reported scaling suspended.
autoscaler-bot: alert: eu-west-1 queue > 100 for 7m, scaling suspended (quota reached). https://internal.metrics/alerts/4652
Maria: cost note — streaming holds a GPU longer which inflates $/request. observed unit-cost for streaming ~2x for similar token counts because of idle wait for new tokens. this matters for dedicated/reserved billing.
Justin: pseudo admission controller sketch:
```
if is_streaming(req):
  est_hold = estimate_hold(req)   # seconds based on historic token pace
  required_slots = ceil(est_hold / SLOT_WINDOW)
  if free_slots >= required_slots and tenant_prio >= MIN_PRIO:
    admit()
  else:
    if allow_degrade: return non_streaming_chunked()
    else: enqueue_with_deadline(req)
else: admit_normal(req)
```
Kevin: +1. also think we should add a "streaming_burst_quota" per-tenant to cap single tenant from monopolizing slots during traffic spikes.
Ashley: practical fallback: start by rate-limiting streaming at ingress by tenant for eu-west for the next 6 hours, move long-tail streamers to chunked responses, and surface metrics per-tenant. can we toggle via feature-flag?
Maria: yes, feature-flaggable config exists in admission service (admission.streaming.priority_mode). we can add an operator toggle to switch from "permit" -> "degrade" -> "block".
Justin: I'll draft a small change to admission-service + telemetry hooks. plan: canary in staging (eu-west-sim) for 24h, then grad rollout. simple dashboards: streaming_hold_time, queue_len_by_lane, tenant_stream_quota_used.
ops-oncall-bot: suggestion: temporary mitigation — enable streaming_degrade for low-priority tenants, add token-based grooming job to close stale open streams after 60s idle.
Kevin: can we preempt low-priority streaming sessions when high-priority non-stream requests arrive? preemption + resume might be tricky for callers but worth discussing.
Maria: preemption could be implemented as soft-preempt (send partial close + resume token) rather than hard-kill. must coordinate in SDKs.
Ashley: next steps: Justin opens PR with flag + metrics, ops flips degrade in eu-west for 6h, infra files quota request with cloud provider. I’ll notify support to throttle tenant-level streaming for impacted customers.
Justin: will do. pinging infra to escalate quota: @infra-team
Ashley: thanks — marking this as action and will follow up in #incidents if it becomes a broader outage. :thumbsup:
